heroHeadline: JNIM Kills 30–50+ in Twin Mopti Village Massacres as Multi-Theater Campaign Continues; FAMa Counter-Operation Kills ~12 Fighters
heroSubtitle: JNIM simultaneously raided Korikori and Gomossogou villages in Mali's Mopti Region on the night of May 6–7, 2026 (reported May 8), killing at least 30–50+ civilians in retaliation against the Dan Na Ambassagou self-defense militia cooperating with FAMa. The attacks demonstrate JNIM's sustained multi-theater capacity: Bamako siege tactics, Kenieroba prison assault, and Mopti massacres all within the same 72-hour operational window. FAMa launched a targeted counter-operation killing approximately 12 JNIM fighters. Burkina Faso signed a counterterrorism cooperation agreement with Somalia on May 7–8, part of the AES bloc's South-South security partnership strategy. The UN OHCHR 'gravely concerning' alert over post-offensive extrajudicial killings remains in force. International analysts published major strategic assessments on May 9 marking the conflict's trajectory as an unprecedented collapse of Malian state authority.
footerNote: Data sourced from ACLED, RFI, Le Monde, Crisis Group, UN OHCHR, HRW, SIPRI, AFP, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, Reuters, Long War Journal, Africa Center for Strategic Studies, Institute for Economics & Peace, US Embassy Bamako, FAO, WFP, Chatham House, PBS NewsHour, Gulf News, WAMAPS, African Arguments, Council on Foreign Relations, Hiiraan Online, Dawan Africa, and Pravda Burkina Faso.
